_comment: Capability-root manifest for workflow/ (founder ruling oyatie-0s8). This is the ADR-0562 capability's OWN service manifest, the `<root>/manifest.json` shape that ci/facade/service-tier-metadata treats as top-level. It exists because the capability-first rehome left 48 of the 48 crates directly under workflow/ belonging to NO manifest: the sub-service manifests under workflow/*/manifest.json cover their own services only. Every crate, service, count and SLO path below was read off the tree, not transcribed.
dr_tier_derivation: Strictest dr_tier declared by any absorbed service of this capability (forms=T1, tasks=T0, workflow-engine=T2, workflow-studio=T0). The shared crates sit in the failure path of the strictest consumer, so the capability root may not claim a weaker DR class than the service that depends on it.

substrate_dag_position._note: ADR-0562 capability-registry declares workflow tier=substrate stratum=S4. depends_on is the UNION of the absorbed service manifests, all four of which declare the identical set. It was empty, which erased every workflow substrate edge for any DAG projection or operational ordering that reads the capability root instead of the per-service manifests — the root is strictly more depended-upon than its parts, never less.

purpose: Workflow orchestration substrate capability root. The crates directly under workflow/ are the capability-level execution-engine, state-machine, trigger-orchestrator and event-bus model, its port/REST/SDK/worker boundaries, its seven event-bus transport adapters (Kafka, NATS, Pulsar, Redpanda, Valkey, Postgres, generic) and its studio/forms/tasks facades. The deployed workflow services (forms, tasks, workflow-engine, workflow-studio) carry their own manifests and SLOs.

bounded_contexts.name: workflow-adapters
bounded_contexts.description: Capability-level driven adapters (storage, transport, provider) under workflow/adapters/.

bounded_contexts.name: workflow-core
bounded_contexts.description: Capability-level domain / usecase / kernel crates (pure, no I/O) under workflow/core/.

bounded_contexts.name: workflow-facade
bounded_contexts.description: Capability-level composition, app and evidence crates under workflow/facade/.

bounded_contexts.name: workflow-ports
bounded_contexts.description: Capability-level port + API boundary crates under workflow/ports/.

capability_root_accounting._overlap_note: COMPUTED, not asserted. No crate under this capability root is declared by any absorbed service manifest, so the whole crate set below was unowned before this file.
capability_root_accounting._divergence_note: dr_tier diverges across the absorbed services (forms=T1, tasks=T0, workflow-engine=T2, workflow-studio=T0), so this flag is true. It was false while those same records carried three distinct values, which let a consumer skip the reconciliation dr_tier_derivation says is required and read the classifications as unanimous. tier_subtype and stratum ARE unanimous; the flag covers any facet.

contracts_non_claim: This capability root serves no endpoint of its own, so all three carrier arrays are EMPTY rather than populated: every OpenAPI, AsyncAPI and proto contract under workflow/ belongs to one of the absorbed services listed above and is declared by that service's manifest. The internal_grpc block is present-and-empty, not omitted, because the H2/proto3 posture binds any internal gRPC this capability may later expose (ADR-0056/0105 zero-GraphQL, internal-only Protobuf); an omitted block would read as an unruled surface.

adrs.title: Closed Capability Registry And Deterministic Placement

sharding_automation.non_claim: A capability root of library crates has no tenant shards to split, merge or rebalance. Sharding automation is claimed by the absorbed services that actually run, in their own manifests; ADR-0348 automation is declared disabled here rather than omitted so the absence is a measured statement instead of a gap.

dr.non_claim: No runtime store, failover drill or DR evidence belongs to this capability root; DR is exercised by the absorbed services. `dr_tier` above is the inherited obligation, not a measured result.

foundation_non_claims: this manifest describes the 48 crates directly under workflow/ and does NOT restate, aggregate or supersede the 4 absorbed service manifests listed above
no deployed process, served endpoint, measured benchmark, capacity telemetry or audit-chain writer is claimed for the capability root itself

slo_exemption.rationale: The workflow/core, workflow/ports, workflow/adapters and workflow/facade crates are capability-level libraries and transport adapters with no deployed process of their own, so no measured runtime SLI exists for them; the four deployed workflow services carry their own OpenSLO files under workflow/observability/slos/. This root manifest is an accounting surface for the shared crates, not a restatement of service SLO coverage.
slo_exemption.evidence: workflow/observability/slos/ — the capability's OpenSLO files all sit under a per-service subdirectory there, none at capability level, which is the measured statement that no SLI belongs to the root crates
